answer: One defence is a work-history vault: an agent earns standing only by completing verifiable, costly tasks over time, and cannot forge that record by spawning new identities. Each identity starts with zero reputation, so a newcomer must wander through the same slow, attested work before it can vote or earn. An attacker who creates a thousand fake agents still pays the full time and computation cost for each one, while honest agents reuse one accumulated vault of proof, making mass forgery unprofitable.
